preview: Aakash Parmar shares his successful interview experience for the 2022 Summer Internship at Samsung R&D Bangalore, detailing the online coding assessment and technical interview rounds.
content: Samsung R&D Bangalore (SRIB) Interview Experience Aakash Parmar | T.Y. B.Tech IT 2019-23 For 2022 Summer Internship (On-campus) R&D Intern 18th February 2022 Samsung R&D Bangalore (SRIB) visited our campus for virtual onboarding for Internship Opportunities. There were 2 rounds in total. 1. Online Coding Skill Assessment Round 2. Online Technical Interview A total of 128 students had applied for this. Round 1: Online Coding Skill Assessment Round The coding round was hosted on cocubes.com in which we had to code 3 problems having 2 sample test cases with the further test cases to be tested in the background (not visible to us) within 70 minutes. Important(For C++) ● STL Algorithms were not allowed. ● STL Containers were allowed. The questions in my set were: 1. Minimum number of boxes required to collect all stones. Given an array containing weights of stones, and an integer K representing maximum weight a box can contain (All boxes are uniform). Each box carries at most 2 stones at the same time, provided the sum of the weight of those stones is at the most limit of the box. The task is to find the minimum number of boxes required to collect all stones. Example: A = [1,2,3,4,5] K = 6 One Possible way to collect all stones: Number of boxes required: 4 Best way to collect all stones: Number of boxes required: 3 Here minimum is 3 so you need to return 3. First I sorted the array using the merge sort as STL algorithms were not allowed then I used two pointers method to get the minimum number of boxes required. 2. All levels LinkedList from the given tree. Given two integers min and max denoting lowest and highest level of a tree and a tree was given. You need to return the head of the LinkedList of nodes that are within the given level of the tree. Example: Low = 2 High = 4 The output should be: 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 -> NULL Firstly I gathered all the nodes which are within the given level using level order traversal of the tree then I created a LinkedList from it. While creating the LinkedList from the gathered nodes I used the sentinel node technique so that for hidden TC’s I don't get TLE. 3. Overlap Binary Tree Given two binary trees tree1 and tree2. We need to overlap tree2 to tree1. The overlap rule was defined as follows: If two nodes overlap, then the node value will be of tree2 otherwise, the non-null node will be used as the node of the new tree. Example: Given two trees. The output tree should be: (You need to return the root of the new tree.) I used DFS to solve this problem. Basically traverse both the trees in the same order and if we have the node for tree2 then the output node would contain the same value as tree2 else will attach the non-null node to the tree. My recursive solution: TreeNode* overlap(TreeNode* tree1, TreeNode* tree2){ if(!tree1)return tree2; if(!tree2)return tree1; tree2->left = overlap(tree1->left,tree2->left); tree2->right = overlap(tree1->right,tree2->right); return tree2; } After 2 days results came and 2 students were shortlisted for the next round. ROUND 2: Online Technical Interview (Deep Interview) This round was on Google Meet and lasted for 1 hour 20 minutes. He started the interview with basic questions to calm me down - 1. How was your day till now? 2. Are you nervous? Then he asked me to introduce myself to which he was listening with great attention (unlike my previous interviews). So this interview was divided into 2 sections: 1. Predict the output / OOPS Questions 2. DSA Questions Predict the output / OOPS Questions: Talking about the difficulty of this section I feel to answer these questions one must require a great understanding of OOPS as they were a bit tricky. MCQs were in the language C/C++ as in the staring he asked whether I am familiar with C/C++. The interviewer had shared his screen and I have to answer the questions one by one and discuss something whenever required. The total number of questions asked was around 12-15. I will list down all the questions which I remember. Question 1: char c = 257; printf(“%d”,c); Question 2: A question based on enums in C. The crux of this problem was that the values in enums start from 0. Question 3: cout << 5||2|1; Question 4: Given Hybrid Inheritance and integers take 4 bytes of space. Child3 ch3; cout << sizeof(ch3); Answer: 20 Bytes. This is a very famous diamond problem in C++. Follow up: How to solve this problem? Answer: Using virtual keyword. Question 5: A question on constructors/destructors in C++. Order of constructor call in multi-level inheritance. What are destructors and the need for them? Question 6: Questions on virtual and pure virtual functions in C++. This section ended in 20-25 minutes. DSA Questions 1. A constructive algorithm based on hashmap. 2. https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-substring-without-repeating-characters 3. https://leetcode.com/problems/product-of-array-except-self (without division ‘/’ operator) 4. https://leetcode.com/problems/kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst 5. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/kth-largest-element-in-bst-when-modification-to-bst-is-not-allowed 6. https://leetcode.com/problems/median-of-two-sorted-arrays In every question, they want the best time and space complexity possible. Then finally he asked do I have any questions for him then I asked him 2-3 questions about the role and after that interview ended. After two days results came and they selected 1 student and I was fortunate enough to be that one.!! Advice: 1. Prepare trees well for clearing the first round of Samsung. 2. Always ask the questions to your interviewer at the end. 3. Be confident throughout the interview (this is very important). 4. Do not get demotivated by the failure/rejection. I learned a lot from my rejections and eventually, you will also learn. 5. Back your skills and keep faith in yourself. ALL THE BEST !
